item.title: Government Websites Go Dark As Vulnerabilities in Programming Language Send Shudder Across Internet
item.description: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators scrambling to protect their systems. Developers of the PHP programming language said Tuesday they had identified two critical vulnerabilities and urged users to update their sites as soon as a fix was released. With reports that hackers were already exploiting the flaws to break into websites, government agencies in the Netherlands and Finland were among those that took sites offline as a precaution.

item.title: LA Fire Victims Set to Lose Case Managers Due to Standoff Between California, FEMA
item.description: Now Landau is one of roughly 1,400 households affected by the 2025 Los Angeles fires who are set to lose their disaster case managers by the end of October, as a standoff between California and the Federal Emergency Management Agency over the program’s funding drags on. Case managers simplify a notoriously opaque recovery process Landau kept her insurance policy up to date for the 1938 two-bedroom, one-bathroom ranch home where she raised her three children and tended a wildflower garden. Much of what has sustained her is the encouragement she receives from her disaster case manager.

item.title: OpenAI President Urges AI Safeguards While Group He Funds Opposes Regulation
item.description: OpenAI President Greg Brockman was among the group of six tech executives who later signed US President Donald Trump’s voluntary AI safety agreement on behalf of their companies, agreeing to work with “independent auditors” and to ensure their AI tools do not “hack or access technical systems in unintended ways.” Yet Leading the Future, a political group backed with a $25 million donation from Brockman and his wife, Anna, opposes regulations that “unduly constrain or delay AI development” in the US. As OpenAI executives step up their public calls for federal AI safety rules, a political group the company’s president helped fund is spending millions to elect members of Congress who oppose restrictions on the technology. “There are leaders in industry who want to pay lip service to regulation because they realize where public opinion is,” said Charlie Blaettler of Guardrails Alliance, a political group formed to counter Leading the Future.

item.title: Vehicle Finance Fraud Now a $10.4B Industry: NICB
item.description: “Vehicle finance fraud has evolved from isolated credit misrepresentations into an organized, digital criminal industry that touches dealerships, lenders and insurers,” said NICB Chief Operating Officer Timothy R. “Stopping these networks requires shifting away from reactive, siloed defenses toward standardized and synchronized cross-industry reporting.” Recent industry studies indicate that up to 24% of all auto loan defaults may be linked to fraud, with 77% of auto dealerships reporting an increase in fraudulent activity over the past two years, the NICB noted. First party fraud, in which individuals or fraud rings misrepresent income, employment, or repayment intent using their own or synthetic identities, now accounts for nearly 70% of all vehicle finance fraud.

item.title: ‘Weird And Maybe Uninvestable’: How Reach Capital Spots Its Venture Winners
item.description: The Reach Capital partner began his career as a high school math teacher with Teach For America after studying astrophysics at Yale . As a teacher, he was an early user of ClassDojo , an experience he describes as “game-changing.” His investment firm, Reach Capital, has also evolved. He later worked in college access and Yale admissions, and earned graduate degrees in business and education from Stanford before joining Reach.

item.title: When A Startup Sells, Its Employees’ Equity Plans Can Change Overnight
item.description: For employees holding equity compensation, a transaction can also change personal financial plans they had expected to follow for years. A client whose employer was acquired in an all-cash transaction described to me the atmosphere inside the company during the weeks that followed: Employees repeatedly discussed the deal in office corridors, trying to understand what it meant for their equity awards, their jobs and their future. Technology employees with substantial equity compensation often depend on their employer in several ways.

item.title: Hamilton returns with $250m target to upsize and renew Easton Re catastrophe bond
item.description: Hamilton Insurance Group has returned to renew its catastrophe bond and we’re told by sources is looking to upsize on the protection it provides, seeking $250 million or more in collateralized multi-peril retrocessional reinsurance from an Easton Re Ltd. Hamilton Insurance Group, the Bermuda based insurance and reinsurance holding company, first entered the catastrophe bond market back in 2020, when it sponsored the $150 million Easton Re Pte. With that Easton Re 2024-1 catastrophe bond scheduled to mature in early January 2027, we understand that Hamilton is back and looking to grow its cat bond protection while renewing it for a further three years.

item.title: There’s a lot of hungry and extremely naive capacity available: Chubb CEO Greenberg
item.description: Competitive insurance and reinsurance market conditions are spreading beyond just property risks, as there is “a lot of hungry and extremely naive capacity available,” Chubb CEO Evan Greenberg said today. “Beyond property, competitive market conditions are spreading to more casualty lines, where pricing in numerous areas is failing to keep pace with loss costs, which, while steady, continue to well-outpace general inflation.” Then he added that, “There is a lot of hungry and extremely naive capacity available. After the second-quarter, Greenberg had said that Chubb has been buying more reinsurance this year as it sees an opportunity to, as he termed it, “feed the hungry” in the competitive and softened market environment .

item.title: Korra launches Deal Analysis to help ILS investors evaluate risk and transaction economics
item.description: Analysis and forecasted results can then be packaged into investor-ready reports, giving teams a consistent way to communicate the assumptions, economics and potential outcomes of a transaction.” Korra also clarified that once a deal goes live, both the data and insights generated during its initial evaluation are carried forward in the platform and then made available as claims develop, thereby facilitating sustained monitoring of deal and portfolio performance alongside continuous reassessment of the transaction structure, while simultaneously enabling more strategically informed decisions regarding contract renewal. Korra, the Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform from Ledger Investing, has announced that it has launched Korra Deal Analysis, an application that’s expected to help market participants analyse the quantitative and qualitative aspects of casualty, non-catastrophe property, and specialty reinsurance and ILS opportunities. According to the announcement, Korra’s Deal Analysis application will enable ceding insurers, reinsurers, managing general agents (MGAs), fronting carriers, and the reinsurance brokers who represent them to structure, price, and publish formal risk and investment reports for their own marketing purposes.

item.title: HCI’s reinsurance tower and token affected after claims from Hurricane Isaias hit
item.description: HCI Group, Inc., a Tampa-based insurance holding company with operations in homeowners insurance, information technology services, real estate, and reinsurance, has confirmed that only one of its three reinsurance towers has been impacted after receiving claims from Hurricane Isaias. The firm said, “Anything above this number will be subject to the company’s reinsurance agreements.” Additionally, taking a look at HCI’s reinsurance tokens, only Token B is expected to be impacted by Hurricane Isaias, which remains profitable despite this hit. At this time, we are focused on supporting our policyholders by processing their claims as efficiently and effectively as possible.” Most recently, catastrophe risk modeller Moody’s RMS Event Response estimated total US private market insured losses from Hurricane Isaias to range from $2.5-4.5 billion , with a best estimate of $3.5 billion.

item.title: Corgi appoints James Kullman as Head of Underwriting, North America
item.description: Corgi Insurance, an AI-native insurance carrier built for high-growth companies, has announced the appointment of James Kullman as Head of Underwriting, North America. In his new role, Kullman will lead efforts to advance commercial underwriting across North America, leveraging AI to improve risk selection, develop underwriting guidelines, strengthen portfolio management and support regulatory compliance. He joins Corgi from Chubb, where he served as Assistant Vice President and Pacific North Region Underwriting Manager for the North American Small and Lower Middle Market.

item.title: Lots of “hungry and naive capacity” in the market as pricing pressures mount: Chubb’s Greenberg
item.description: “There is a lot of hungry and extremely naive capacity available,” Evan Greenberg, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Chubb, highlighted as he addressed mounting competitive pressures across global commercial property and casualty (P&C) lines. Pointing to an influx of undisciplined underwriting capacity, Greenberg noted that Chubb’s global reach remains its strongest shield: “Our broad diversification, including a deep local presence in so many countries and lines of business, leave us relatively well positioned with many areas of opportunity.” The executive noted that pricing conditions across commercial P&C markets, most notably in the United States and London, are becoming increasingly aggressive. “Beyond property competitive market conditions are spreading to more casualty lines where pricing in numerous areas is failing to keep pace with lost costs, which while steady continue to well outpace general inflation,” Greenberg stated.

item.title: Storm Austen Will Be Stronger Than Forecast Along UK Coasts
item.description: Britain’s first named storm of the autumn will be stronger than previously thought when it sweeps across the country later this week. Gusts from Storm Austen may reach 80 miles (129 kilometers) per hour in coastal areas, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the five-step Saffir-Simpson scale, according to the UK Met Office. If that occurs, it would be a sign that Austen is a “rapidly intensifying, potent storm” with destructive potential, Pedrini said.

item.title: 23andMe Settles for $6 Million Over California Data Breach
item.description: The 2023 data breach affected nearly 7 million 23andMe customers nationwide, including more than 855,000 Californians, according to the California DOJ, which launched an investigation that year. Related: California Cannot Seek Damages From 23andMe Successor Over 2023 Data Breach The agreement also resolves an appeal by the California DOJ over the sale of genetic information and biological samples during 23andMe’s bankruptcy proceedings without customers’ consent. Chrome Holding Co., formerly 23andMe, reached a $6 million settlement to resolve allegations that the genetic testing company failed to protect personal information and genetic data of customers in a 2023 data breach.

item.title: Global Insured Catastrophe Losses Fall to Lowest 9-Month Level Since 2019: Report
item.description: Global economic losses (which include both insured and uninsured losses) reached US$242 billion during the nine-month period, which marked the lowest Q1-Q3 total since 2015 and was around 33% lower than the 10-year Q1-Q3 average, the report said. Global insured losses from natural catastrophes reached US$92 billion during the first nine months of 2026, 29% below the 10-year average (US$128 billion) and the lowest year-to-date insured loss total since 2019, according to Gallagher Re. The insurance industry has now experienced six consecutive quarters without a single natural catastrophe event generating more than US$10 billion in insured losses, representing one of the longest such stretches in decades, said Gallagher Re’s Q3 2026 Natural Catastrophe and Climate Report .

item.title: Aviva Insurance Ireland and insureMO to launch new embedded insurance proposition across Europe
item.description: The post Aviva Insurance Ireland and insureMO to launch new embedded insurance proposition across Europe appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Aviva Insurance Ireland DAC and insureMO, a global provider of insurance middle office platforms, have announced a new partnership to deliver embedded insurance solutions across Aviva’s European business, making protection simpler, more relevant, and easier for customers to access. The launch supports Aviva’s strategy to expand embedded insurance solutions across Europe.

item.title: SoFi partners with Prudential
item.description: SoFi and Prudential Financial announced a partnership that will give over 15 million SoFi members the ability to purchase Prudential term life insurance directly within the SoFi app. Through a fully digital experience built and operated by SoFi, members can explore Prudential’s SimplyTerm life insurance, receive an instant quote, and apply for and purchase coverage in one place. Available through the SoFi app, the embedded experience streamlines the application process and reduces redundant data entry, with eligible members often able to obtain coverage in minutes without a medical exam or lab work.

item.title: Root launches in Wyoming
item.description: Root Insurance is now available in Wyoming, expanding its auto insurance availability to 38 states representing 81% of the U.S. “Launching in Wyoming brings us another step closer to making Root available to drivers across the country. Root plans to offer coverage across the contiguous United States by the end of 2027.

item.title: SageSure adds Olympus capacity for higher-value California homes
item.description: SageSure has expanded its SageSure One homeowners program in California with capacity from Olympus Insurance Company, offering up to $20 million in total insurable value. Olympus joins SURE and SafePort as carriers supporting SageSure One’s California offerings. It targets higher-value properties positioned between mass-market homeowners insurance and high-net-worth offerings.

item.title: Instacart Settling Probe Over Foreign Worker Recruiting for $5 Million
item.description: Instacart parent Maplebear will pay $5 million to settle a federal investigation into claims that the grocery delivery company discriminated against American workers through its recruiting and hiring practices, two U.S. Department of Justice and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission said they had uncovered evidence that Instacart preferred to hire foreign workers through an employment-based green card program rather than Americans for unspecified jobs. President Donald Trump, a Republican, has sought to crack down on what he says are widespread abuses of foreign worker visa programs.

item.title: Former chief executive banned after misconduct led to £4m losses in high-risk investments
item.description: The FCA has banned Jeffrey Dawkins, the former chief executive of Vector Wealth Ltd, after he dishonestly acted as a front for a disqualified director using the company to sell high-risk bonds. Therese Chambers, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said, 'Jeffrey Dawkins acted as a front man for a banned director, helping high-risk investments look safer than they were. Mini-bonds and similar investments are very high risk, and people should be extremely cautious.' The FCA has warned about the risks of investing in mini-bonds and loan notes.

item.title: 44% of Policyholders Say How They Pay Helps Decide Who Insures Them
item.description: Policyholders wanted to use digital wallets at 34%, but only 20% of insurers offered them. Preferred payment options were a reason to choose an insurance provider for 44% of policyholders, PYMNTS Intelligence found. The payment experience plays a role in how consumers choose a property or home insurer, not just how they pay once a policy is in place.

item.title: Gallagher Re estimates global insured cat losses at $92bn for 9M’26, lowest since 2019
item.description: Insured losses from natural catastrophe events across the globe during the first nine months of 2026 are estimated to have reached US $92 billion, representing the lowest total for the first nine months of a year since 2019, and 29% below the 10-year average of $128 billion, according to reinsurance broker Gallagher Re’s Q3 2026 Natural Catastrophe and Climate Report. The image below, taken from Gallagher Re’s latest report, highlights how 2026 continues to run below the 10-year average for both insured and economic losses, while the United States contributes 62% of global insured losses to-date in 2026. At the same time, the broker noted that severe convective storms (SCS) generated at least $43 billion in insured losses in the United States alone during Q3 2026, while on a global basis, SCS accounted for nearly 60% of all insured catastrophe losses during the first three-quarters of the year.

item.title: USAA lifts Residential Re 2026-2 cat bond target to $350m as price guidance drops
item.description: USAA is aiming to upsize its latest catastrophe bond issuance by 56% and secure the protection at reduced pricing, as the insurer now targets $350 million of collateralized multi-peril catastrophe reinsurance from the Residential Reinsurance 2026 Limited (Series 2026-2) issuance, Artemis understands. USAA is still the most consistent and long-standing catastrophe bond sponsor in the marketplace, having added to and diversified its sources of catastrophe reinsurance protection using the capital markets since the beginning of cat bonds back in 1997 and this Residential Re 2026-2 issuance set to become the 48th cat bond for USAA that we have analysed and tracked. The Residential Reinsurance 2026 Limited special purpose vehicle is offering three tranches of Series 2026-2 occurrence catastrophe bond notes to investors, with the proceeds set to be used to collateralize underlying reinsurance agreements between the issuing vehicle and sponsor USAA.

item.title: Hannover Re targets 75% upsized $350m of limit from new Acorn Re parametric cat bond
item.description: Hannover Re’s seventh catastrophe bond offering in the annual Acorn Re parametric US earthquake series of deals looks set to grow, as the target size for this issuance has been raised by 75% to now seek $350 million of limit from the Acorn Re Ltd. Hannover Re returned to market with this new and now seventh Acorn Re parametric catastrophe bond earlier this month , initially seeking $200 million of risk transfer and reinsurance limit for the single named ceding insurer, Oak Tree Assurance Ltd. These parametric catastrophe bonds, under the Acorn Re series, play a kind of dual role in protecting Oak Tree Assurance, a Vermont-based workers compensation captive insurer of the Kaiser Permanente group of health plan companies, while also providing a type of retrocessional reinsurance for Hannover Re to protect other reinsureds that might face losses under the cat bond’s trigger conditions.

item.title: Holborn names Manus as CEO and Releford as President in leadership succession
item.description: Holborn Corporation has announced the next phase of its leadership succession, with Frank Harrison to retire as CEO and continue as Non-Executive Chairman, Adam Manus to become CEO, and Tim Releford to become President, effective 1 March 2027. In their new leadership roles, Manus and Releford will remain directly involved with clients and work alongside Holborn’s broking teams on client accounts. The Holborn Way will not.” Both Manus and Releford have spent their entire professional careers at the independent reinsurance broker and together bring approximately 55 years of Holborn experience to their new positions.

item.title: Arbol launches first-of-its-kind cover for data centre regulatory moratorium risk
item.description: Arbol, the AI-native insurer, has launched a Data Center Regulatory Moratorium Cover, a first-of-its-kind product that transfers the risk of government action halting or suspending data centre construction. “Data centre development has a new and fast-growing risk, and until now there was no way to transfer it,” said Sid Jha, founder and CEO of Arbol. This type of regulatory risk has long been considered uninsurable, with the cover addressing a gap not covered by existing policies.

item.title: Thomas Blunck takes over Munich Re’s Europe and Latin America P&C reinsurance business
item.description: Munich Re has appointed Thomas Blunck to take responsibility for its Property and Casualty (P&C) Reinsurance business in Europe and Latin America, effective 1 November 2026. Blunck, who will continue in his role as CEO of Reinsurance, will assume the additional responsibility from Clarisse Kopff, who will step down from the Board of Management of Munich Reinsurance Company by mutual agreement at the end of 31 October 2026. During his time on the board, he has held a range of responsibilities across the group, including Special and Financial Risks, Europe and Latin America, and Life and Health.

item.title: Alabama Pharmacy, Not Agent, at Fault for Not Reading Policy Before $5M Judgment
item.description: An Alabama insurance agent is in the clear after years of litigation that contended he had failed to secure professional liability coverage for a pharmacy that was sued over a compounded medication error. The Alabama pharmacy owner had contributed to the oversight by failing to carefully read his own insurance policy, the Alabama Supreme Court said in a recent opinion in OMS Pharmacy v. The suit against Nationwide and Baldo-Downs Insurance, a Tuscaloosa agency, and Roger Downs, the head of the predecessor agency, stemmed from a nearly $5 million judgment against OMS Pharmacy.

item.title: EC-Council Acquires Cyber Insurance Academy, Expands AI Risk Education
item.description: Cyber insurance will remain the Academy’s core focus while its capabilities expand into three areas: AI risk, emerging technology risk and role-based technology education for insurance professionals. The acquisition will allow the Academy to expand beyond cyber insurance into AI risk, emerging technology exposures and technology education for brokers, underwriters, claims professionals and risk managers. The acquisition gives Cyber Insurance Academy access to EC-Council’s technical expertise, global network and cybersecurity and AI capabilities, while EC-Council gains a dedicated insurance education business with established industry relationships and credentialing expertise.

item.title: WR Berkley CEO Shares Insights on AI Adoption During Q3 Call
item.description: “My colleagues many, many years ago recognized the importance of data and how that role was going to become ever more greater,” he said in his opening remarks during a conference call to discuss Q3 earnings. chose the third quarter of 2026 to enlighten analysts on the insurer’s journey parallel to society’s breakneck adoption of technological advances and its effect on the economy. Data is the fuel that drives those engines.” Initially, artificial intelligence brought speed to the specialty insurer’s underwriting and claims, Berkley explained.

item.title: Chubb posts record $5.79bn P&C underwriting income for first nine months of 2026
item.description: The post Chubb posts record $5.79bn P&C underwriting income for first nine months of 2026 appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Chubb has reported record property and casualty (P&C) underwriting income of $5.79bn for the first nine months of 2026, up 33.7% year on year, with a P&C combined ratio of 84%. “For the first nine months of the year, which is a more meaningful perspective, core operating income is a record $8.6 billion, or $21.94 per share, up 21% and 24.5%, respectively, from the prior year,” said Greenberg.

item.title: King Risk Partners adds two Florida professional liability specialists
item.description: King Risk Partners has acquired two Florida agencies specialising in professional liability and cyber insurance for professional services firms: Risk Avoidance Managers of St. By buying two established specialists rather than building the capability itself, King Risk Partners gains carrier relationships and expertise it can offer across its wider network. Both agencies write professional liability and cyber cover for law firms, accounting firms, financial planners, and individual professionals across Florida.

item.title: Kentucky National joins Warrior Insurance Network
item.description: Warrior Insurance Network has added Kentucky National Insurance Company to its network, with plans to retain the insurer’s name and Kentucky identity while expanding its resources and product offerings. Founded in 1973, Kentucky National currently offers preferred personal auto insurance through independent agencies across Kentucky. The companies have begun meeting with Kentucky National’s independent agents to help shape future products and make improvements to existing offerings.

item.title: Skuld restructures underwriting and regional operations
item.description: Marine insurer Skuld is reorganizing its executive team and regional operations, effective November 1, 2026, following growth across products and markets. Chief financial officer Kristian Løberg will become chief underwriting officer, with Oda Bjerketvedt Norderud taking over as CFO. Skuld is also establishing global leadership roles for its core products.

item.title: King Risk Partners acquires two Florida agencies
item.description: King Risk Partners has acquired Risk Avoidance Managers and Coastal Insurors, adding professional liability and cyber insurance expertise in Florida. Both agencies serve individual professionals and professional services firms, including law firms, accounting firms and financial planners throughout Florida. Michael Halfast, a producer for both acquired agencies, said joining King will provide broader capabilities, expanded market access and additional resources for clients.

item.title: Project Eleven, Relm Explore Quantum Risk in Digital Asset Insurance
item.description: (Image source: Project Eleven website.) Project Eleven (New York) has named Relm Insurance a development partner for Strongpoint, its institutional digital asset custody product, as the companies explore how post-quantum security controls could be evaluated within insurance underwriting. Project Eleven says a sufficiently capable quantum computer could eventually derive private keys from exposed public keys, creating a potential threat to digital assets. Bringing Underwriting Into Quantum Readiness Relm and Project Eleven will examine factors including key exposure, signing systems, transaction approvals, migration readiness and third-party dependencies.

item.description: (Image source: IIR.) OWIT Global (West Hartford, Conn.) says a large U.S. carrier is expanding its use of the company’s Insurance Workbench for Bordereaux and Data Management across additional business units. The carrier originally selected OWIT as part of an effort to expand its program business while streamlining MGA and TPA onboarding and data processing.

item.title: Insurer Rolls Out Policy to Protect Data Centers Against Growing Backlash
item.description: Intensifying public pushback against artificial intelligence data centers is spurring a new line of business for a New York-based boutique insurer. Arbol, which was founded by a former Citadel strategist, on Tuesday launched a new policy that protects data center developers and financiers against government-imposed moratoriums that halt or suspend construction. “Data center development has a new and fast-growing risk, and until now there was no way to transfer it,” said Siddhartha Jha, Arbol’s chief executive officer.

item.title: AAA Survey Reveals Disconnect in Drivers’ Obeying ‘Slow Down, Move Over’ Laws
item.description: Though more than 90% of drivers reported moving over and/or slowing down the last time they passed a disabled vehicle, tow truck, or police car on the shoulder, previous AAA FTS research found that only 64% of vehicles subject to Slow Down, Move Over laws were observed changing lanes and/or reducing speed; 36% did neither. We all have a responsibility to keep Roadside Heroes safe as they rescue people.” When Slow Down, Move Over laws were explained, 90% of drivers supported them, and only 2% opposed them. When drivers encounter a vehicle stopped along the roadside, they need to respond right away — because failing to slow down or move over can turn a standard stop into a preventable tragedy.” Closing the gap begins with public education across multiple channels.

item.title: Tech Bytes: New Partnerships at The Zebra, LexisNexis Risk Solutions
item.description: Sources: The Zebra, LexisNexis Risk Solutions LexisNexis Risk Solutions, a provider of data and analytics for the insurance and automotive industries, and IMS, a global connected insurance technology company, announced the integration of the LexisNexis Drive Metrics scoring model into the IMS EdgeSDK. Driving behavior information stays on the user’s device while generating scores and attributes that can be quickly incorporated into existing workflows and are consistent across LexisNexis Telematics Solutions.
